frequency_source: OPUS OpenSubtitles v2024 Luxembourgish frequencies https://object.pouta.csc.fi/OPUS-OpenSubtitles/v2024/freq/lb.freq.gz , supplemented by the Leipzig Luxembourgish Wikipedia 2021 100K word list https://downloads.wortschatz-leipzig.de/corpora/ltz_wikipedia_2021_100K.tar.gz (FrequencyWords 2018 has no lb file).
how_to_tell_apart: Luxembourgish can look like German until ech, ass, net, dat/déi, hunn, moien, äddi, näischt, gëtt, muer and wann ech gelift appear, or until the letter ë is visible. German would have ich, ist, nicht, habe and danke; Dutch would have ik, is, niet and dankjewel; French loans such as merci are common in Luxembourgish and must not be read as proof that the speaker switched to French. Afrikaans ek/nie/dankie are a different West Germanic pair.
test_said: An der Gemeng brauch ech e Wunnsëtzcertificat fir d'Schoul vum Kand.
Zanter haut moies ass de Stroum an der ganzer Trap ausgefall an ech well dat mellen.
De Päckchen an der Post ass ukomm mee ech hunn nach keng Noriicht kritt.
D'Miwwele mussen iwwer d'Trap eropgedroen ginn well den Lift ze kleng ass.
Beim Zänndokter froen ech no engem éischte fräie Termäin well et wéi deet.
D'Bluttanalys sollt donnescht fäerdeg sinn an ech froen ob d'Resultat do ass.
Eng nei Hausversécherung wëll ech net ofschléissen an och keng Donnéeën duerchginn.
De Stroumvertrag gouf dëse Mount geännert dofir brauche mer keng weider Offeren.
uncertain: The OpenSubtitles lb list is relatively small, so greetings such as moien and äddi were confirmed against the larger Leipzig Wikipedia word list as well.
ë is the clearest unique letter versus German; ä also occurs, but German uses ä too.
Spoken Luxembourgish freely mixes French and German content words, which can make a short turn look multilingual even when the grammar is Luxembourgish.
